speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. To better understand your condition, can you tell me when your fever started relative to delivery, and what specific characteristics your abdominal pain has (e.g., location, severity, or radiation)?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has your fever been accompanied by chills or rigors, and have you noticed any foul-smelling lochia or changes in vaginal discharge? Also, when you mention decreased bowel sounds, do you feel any bloating or nausea?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with Differential, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, and Urinalysis/Culture. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound.

Has the uterine tenderness been localized to a specific area, such as the lower abdomen or pelvic region, and is the pain worsening when you press on your abdomen?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Uncomplicated pregnancy leading up to a vaginal delivery. No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: Does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. Lives with her partner.

speaker: Patient
text: Complains of minor difficulty in breathing but denies any urinary pain, headache, vomiting, or diarrhea. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum Uterine Atony with secondary infection and potential urinary retention.

REQUEST TEST: Urine Output Measurement and Bladder Scan. REQUEST IMAGES: Repeat Transabdominal Ultrasound focused on the uterus and bladder.

Please confirm if you have had difficulty passing urine or if your bladder feels full and distended upon palpation.
